Operations managers, dispatch leads — I’m Mike, founder of Slatebridge. Every day, techs call in sick, customers get upset, and SLAs run out. Missed deadlines are usually blamed on people: the dispatcher didn’t route well enough or the tech was too busy with other work.

But what if it’s not always about who is assigned where? What if missed SLAs often come from assignments made without full visibility into travel times, skill sets, and deadlines stacking on each other?

At Slatebridge, we built a system that tracks all these factors. Dispatchers see every technician's available time and the order of their jobs. The plan is done before the dispatcher finishes their coffee. This means the right techs are always assigned to the right jobs, even when last-minute changes happen.

The difference? Missed SLAs go from a people problem to a data management one. Instead of chasing the blame, dispatchers can focus on optimizing routes and training technicians better.

So, what do you think? Have you faced missed SLAs that seemed more scheduling than tech capacity issues?
